text: They are queued as they arrive, and then there is a server that is just a function that serves these packets one by one in the same order as they arrive. Okay? If you queue these packets according to the order in which they arrive, we say that this queue works in a FIFO manner, that is, first input, first output. So who arrives first will be served first, and we get out first, right? So let's assume that we have this FIFO queue. So our Mac layer, when we have the transmitter, we can model the Mac as a queue, right? Where packets arrive, they are queued in a FIFO according to the FIFO policy, and then the function that is implemented at the Mac layer, we will serve these packets one at a time, and a packet finishes to be served when it gets out and can proceed to the physical layer. Okay? So this is I think a very useful way to think of how our Mac layer works. Okay.
